# google_config_deployment_group

A collection of DeploymentUnits in a DAG-like structure.


To get more information about DeploymentGroup, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/infrastructure-manager/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.deploymentGroups)

## Example Usage - Config Deployment Group Basic


```hcl
resource "google_config_deployment_group" "default" {
  name     = "my-deployment-group"
  location = "us-central1"

  deployment_units {
    id         = "unit-1"
    deployment = google_config_deployment.deployment.id
  }
}

resource "google_config_deployment" "deployment" {
  name            = "my-deployment"
  location        = "us-central1"
  service_account = "projects/my-project/serviceAccounts/my-service-account@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"

  terraform_blueprint {
    git_source {
      repo      = "https://github.com/terraform-google-modules/terraform-google-network"
      directory = "modules/vpc"
      ref       = "main"
    }

    input_values {
      variable_name = "project_id"
      input_value   = "my-project"
    }
    input_values {
      variable_name = "network_name"
      input_value   = "my-network"
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `name` -
  (Required)
  The user-specified ID of the deployment group.

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location for the resource


* `deployment_units` -
  (Optional)
  The deployment units of the deployment group in a DAG like structure.
  When a deployment group is being provisioned, the deployment units are
  deployed in a DAG order.
  The provided units must be in a DAG order, otherwise an error will be
  returned.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_deployment_units).

* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  User-defined metadata for the deployment group.
  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.

* `annotations` -
  (Optional)
  Arbitrary key-value metadata storage.
  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_annotations` for all of the annotations present on the resource.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
* `deployment_reference_policy` - (Optional) Policy on how to handle referenced deployments when deleting the DeploymentGroup.

* `force_destroy` - (Optional) If set to true, any revisions for this deployment group will also be deleted.
(Otherwise, the request will only work if the deployment group has no revisions.)



<a name="nested_deployment_units"></a>The `deployment_units` block supports:

* `id` -
  (Required)
  The id of the deployment unit. Must be unique within the deployment group.

* `dependencies` -
  (Optional)
  The IDs of the deployment units within the deployment group that this
  unit depends on.

* `deployment` -
  (Optional)
  The name of the deployment to be provisioned.
  Format:
  'projects/{project_id}/locations/{location}/deployments/{deployment}'.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/deploymentGroups/{{name}}`

* `create_time` -
  Output only. Time when the deployment group was created.

* `update_time` -
  Output only. Time when the deployment group was last updated.

* `state` -
  Current state of the deployment group.

* `state_description` -
  Additional information regarding the current state.

* `provisioning_state` -
  The provisioning state of the deployment group.

* `provisioning_state_description` -
  Additional information regarding the current provisioning state.

* `terraform_labels` -
  The combination of labels configured directly on the resource
   and default labels configured on the provider.

* `effective_labels` -
  All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services.

* `effective_annotations` -
  All of annotations (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the annotations configured through Terraform, other clients and services.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


DeploymentGroup can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/deploymentGroups/{{name}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{name}}`
* `{{location}}/{{name}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import DeploymentGroup using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    name = "<-required value->"
    location = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_config_deployment_group.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import DeploymentGroup using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/deploymentGroups/{{name}}"
  to = google_config_deployment_group.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), DeploymentGroup can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_config_deployment_group.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/deploymentGroups/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_config_deployment_group.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_config_deployment_group.default {{location}}/{{name}}
```
